scenes.tts: When the skin of a mouse's hindpaw is indented, what climbs the spinal cord? The textbook draws a cable. Touch spikes enter the dorsal column and run up to the brainstem. Studies in mice show a missing branch. Some of the spikes have already been through the cord's own circuitry.

scenes.tts: One route really is direct. Touch afferents are the sensory fibres from the skin. Some run up the dorsal column with no synapse on the way, and reach the gracile nucleus in the brainstem. In anaesthetized adult mice, this direct input carried vibration with high temporal precision.
scenes.visual: direct blue axon lights up the dorsal column to the gracile box, spikes travel
scenes.narration: One route really is direct. Touch afferents are the sensory fibres from the skin. Some run up the dorsal column with no synapse on the way, and reach the gracile nucleus in the brainstem. In anaesthetized adult mice, this direct input carried vibration with high temporal precision.

scenes.tts: Touch afferents also end in the dorsal horn, a layered region of the cord. The layers are called laminae, numbered from the surface. In the mouse lumbar cord, about seventy percent of the neurons in this zone are excitatory, and about thirty percent are inhibitory. A postsynaptic dorsal column neuron, or P S D C neuron, gets its excitation mainly from these local neurons. It sends an axon up the dorsal column.

scenes.tts: Two kinds of inhibition shape what the P S D C neuron sends. In feedforward inhibition, the same afferent input that excites the neuron also excites an interneuron that inhibits it. In presynaptic inhibition, the inhibition lands on the afferent terminal and turns down the transmitter it releases. In anaesthetized adult mice, a genetic knockout of either one enlarged the receptive fields of these neurons.

scenes.tts: Now compare arrival times, using illustrative numbers. The direct route is zero point zero eight metres at sixteen metres per second. That takes five milliseconds. The indirect route needs two point five milliseconds to reach the cord. Two synapses, at an assumed one millisecond each, add two. The P S D C axon, at an assumed eight metres per second, adds five. The total is nine point five milliseconds, so the processed copy arrives four point five milliseconds later.

scenes.tts: The two copies meet again. In anaesthetized adult mice, the direct and indirect inputs to single thalamus-projecting neurons in the gracile nucleus had highly aligned receptive fields. The direct input carried vibration. The indirect input carried sustained indentation, up to high forces. Both contributed to gentle displacement. So the brainstem receives a direct copy and a processed copy.
scenes.visual: both axons converge on one neuron in the gracile box; aligned receptive field circles
